## Design

### 2026-11-03: Ok so what is brcked? Brcked is a telephone through which you get weird and unhinged advices, and you can even talk with it (even though it may be not so friendly). It will have differnt persons and p

**3.5h**

Ok so what is brcked? Brcked is a telephone through which you get weird and unhinged advices, and you can even talk with it (even though it may be not so friendly). It will have differnt persons and personalities to talk to and i'll try to add more features to it frequently

I started building the schematic of this project. I searches google and ai's on how to get footprints/schematics but i didn't found anything for raspberry, so i searched on how to make it custom and made it for for all.

Now i have completed the main main schematic however the switch matrix and more schematics are still left, that i will be adding after this devlog.

It took me a hell lot of time to do this as i do not have much experience with hardware projects but i think i can pull it off. And that was pretty much it. These are the list of parts:

The Parts most probably that i will be using are (these maybe change based on availability and ability of mine😭):
1) Raspberry pi Zero 2w
2) Inmp441 mic
3) IP5306 power module
4) Max98- amplifier module
5) lipo batteries
6) switch buttons
7) TFT Display

### 2026-11-03: Sat to complete the PCB layout. Already had the schematic settled (kinda), so the focus was purely on routing and layout, placement, trace routing, cleaning things up

**3.3h**

Sat to complete the PCB layout. Already had the schematic settled (kinda), so the focus was purely on routing and layout, placement, trace routing, cleaning things up

(And Assigned footprints as well)

Started with component placement, trying to keep the layout logical and not have traces crossing all over the place. Spent a good chunk of time just moving parts around before committing to actual routing,i kinda had to eyeball it a few times before the layout clicked

After playing here and there once placement felt right,then i moved into actual trace routing. This part ate a ton of my time, had to rip up and redo a few traces that were taking weird paths or getting too close to other components. Kept going back and forth between the PCB editor and schematic to double check nothing was mismatched.

After sometime i got to know i had mislabled the global label for the power module and instead of "5v" i had written "5V" so it caused me trouble for like 10-15 mins as well.

It took me a hell lot of time to beautifully route this board and i think its pretty as well....
